name: FLEdge
description: Federated Learning (FL) has become a viable technique for realizing privacy-enhancing distributed deep learning on the network edge. Heterogeneous hardware, unreliable client devices, and energy constraints often characterize edge computing systems. In this paper, we propose FLEdge, which complements existing FL benchmarks by enabling a systematic evaluation of client capabilities. We focus on computational and communication bottlenecks, client behavior, and data security implications. Our experiments with models varying from 14K to 80M trainable parameters are carried out on dedicated hardware with emulated network characteristics and client behavior. We find that state-of-the-art embedded hardware has significant memory bottlenecks, leading to 4x longer processing times than on modern data center GPUs.
evaluation_method: task_success_rate and resource/performance metrics (processing time, memory usage, throughput)
reputation: Recognized in the federated learning and edge-computing research community as a focused benchmark for hardware and network heterogeneity evaluation, but not a broadly adopted standard like LEAF.
notes: Non-LLM/system-level benchmark focused on runtime and resource metrics; results are hardware- and network-emulation dependent. Emulated client behaviour and hardware-specific bottlenecks limit direct comparability across different experimental setups.
